Read through the https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/54918 thread... 

Yeah, we're not always adding a cni conf file when we expect networking to work. As networking isn't a requirement for all scenarios, we (containerd cri) report the error and let it go. If you add a valid conf file at config.toml defined location, any time before or after running containerd.. we have a watcher that will check it out.. and the next run pod will use the new config.

I see good cni results matching cni setup requests just have to search ahead in the log for the result for that pod when other pods are getting started up at the same time.

digging through the code some more.. the way to get nil on net stats:
https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/ea7a9cbac03ccd8845cedda464ee350c22f1698d/pkg/cri/server/sandbox_stats_linux.go#L72-L83
is not to have a sandbox.NetNSPath and that only happens if there is a failure over here:
https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/ea7a9cbac03ccd8845cedda464ee350c22f1698d/pkg/cri/server/sandbox_run.go#L141-L156
need to match up the failure pod id to a successful cni result

I think we have a much better idea of why this is occurring now. Please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109608#issuecomment-1105922281 for explanation.

In summary, there is a race condition where the pod sandbox infra container has not fully started yet and cAdvisor attempts to query the containerd task api to get the pid of the pause container. This is done because a pid is required to lookup network stats (and we use the pause infra container to report stats for the pod). If the pause container is not fully up, containerd task api will return "uninitialized" `0` for the pid and a nil error. cAdvisor assumes that the task api returned successfully and is later unable to fetch network stats because it does not have the correct pid for the pause container.

This is definitely a bug, but it does not seem like a regression, this code appears to have had this bug for quite a few releases already. We should followup with a fix to make it more resilient to this case and can cherrypick it as appropriate, but I'm not sure if this should be release blocker since it does not appear to be a regression in 1.24.
